newsitem.title: USA: Simpson sees '97 sales on par with '96.
newsitem.headline: Simpson sees '97 sales on par with '96.

text.p: Simpson Industries Inc said Tuesday it expects sales for 1997 to be on a par with the $408 million it achieved last year.

"Industry estimates call for North American light vehicle and diesel engine production to be off slightly this year. We are currently expecting sales for 1997 to be comparable to 1996," said president Roy Parrott in a statement.
"At the same time, we start a strong lineup of 13 new product launches in 1997, but we will post only a partial year of revenues from these programs," Parrott continued.

"A number of these product launches are in the rapidly growing wheel-end and suspension product line. We expect sales growth to pick up beginning in 1998 as this year's launches produce a full year of revenues and more new products come on stream," he said.
Parrott also pointed out that Simpson is actively looking for the best way to enter the European market -- joint venture, acquisition or partnership.

Earlier, Simpson posted fourth-quarter earnings of $0.23 a share on sales of $98.3 million. It said a General Motors Corp strike reduced quarterly sales by about $1.3 million. For the full year, the powertrain and chassis supplier earned $0.97 a share.
